title: Auditable collector buffering and idempotent reconciliation for private usage reporting
creator: Aisha Mehta
description:
Problem: Private/VPC (air-gapped or intermittently-connected) deployments currently buffer metering events locally and upload them in periodic bundles. We have seen 3 classes of correctness failures in customer deployments: (1) duplicate accounting from retries + partial bundle commits, (2) orphaned usage records after partial network failures, and (3) local rate-limit enforcement diverging from the hosted control plane when counters drift. This leads to billing discrepancies, quota surprises, and customer support churn.

Goal: Deliver an auditable, idempotent, and tamper-evident local collector design and reconciliation process such that: (A) any bundle uploaded to the control plane can be applied exactly once, (B) local enforcement (quotas/rate-limits) can operate safely offline and reconcile without over/under-charging, and (C) operators can trace and reconcile mismatches via bundle manifests and a replayable ledger.

Constraints: Must run in air-gapped environments with limited outbound windows, work with existing KMS/HSM integrations, minimize CPU/IO on small on-prem appliances, and avoid major changes to the hosted billing ledger schema.

High-level design summary:
- Each tenant local collector maintains a monotonic per-tenant sequence (monotonic_event_seq) and embeds an idempotency key per usage event derived from tenant+seq+shard.
- Events are grouped into compressed signed bundles (bundle format v2) containing: start_seq, end_seq, merkle_root_of_events, bundle_manifest.json (signed with KMS key), and a compact binary payload.
- Bundles are checkpointed to stable local storage (checkpoint metadata written after fsync). Upload attempts are retried with exponential backoff; server accepts bundle once and returns a canonical bundle_id; collector transitions bundle state to uploaded-once when confirmed.
- Server-side ingestion verifies bundle signature, merkle root, and contiguous sequence ranges. Server is idempotent: replays of the same bundle_id are ignored. Partial-applications are prevented via a two-phase-apply: verify -> reserve -> commit.
- Local quota enforcement uses a shadow-window algorithm: offline quotas are checked using a local soft-counter; when reconciling, any overconsumption is marked as provisional and source-of-truth is server ledger. If server rejects delta due to quota, collector will back-fill compensating negative usage events and flag customer admin.

Success metrics:
- 99.99% reduction in duplicate usage records for private installs over a 90-day window.
- Reconciliation latency (time from bundle upload to ledger commit) < 2 minutes on success path.
- Support tickets related to private billing miscounts reduced by 80% in next quarter.

acceptance_criteria: Collector persists bundles with monotonic sequence and manifest signature.
Server accepts bundles idempotently and rejects non-contiguous or tampered bundles.
Reconciliation job can produce an audit report showing matched bundle_ids, applied event ranges, and any compensating entries.
Console exposes per-tenant last-seen-bundle, upload status, and reconciliation status for admins.
Automated e2e test covers intermittent network with random reboots and validates ledger equals local-sourced sum after reconciliation.
implementation_notes:
Detailed decisions and trade-offs:
1) Sequence vs vector-clock: chose per-tenant monotonic sequence to keep bundle manifests small and server-side merge logic simple. Vector clocks were rejected for complexity and storage overhead.
2) Signatures: require KMS-signed manifests (customer key when available). For air-gapped installs without KMS, bundle will carry an operator-provided keypair and a proof-of-rotation header; security review required (see security_review_required).
3) Checkpointing: use two-phase fsync: write bundle file, write metadata file, fsync metadata. This guarantees bundle won't be detected as uploaded unless checkpointed.
4) Quota enforcement: local soft counters + server reconciliation chosen over fully-disconnected strong enforcement to avoid customer outages under intermittent connectivity. This requires compensating negative events on server when disagreements are detected.
5) Compression: zstd level 3 by default; allow config to tune for CPU constrained appliances.

Open questions:
- How to handle bundles spanning tenant-config changes (e.g., plan downgrade mid-bundle)? Proposal: split bundles at config-change boundary and mark both manifests with prior/after plan id.
- UX: how much history to surface in Console for admins vs keeping sensitive raw bundles in storage?
testing_plan: Unit tests for merkle root and idempotency key generation (collector & server).
Integration tests: simulated intermittent connectivity with deterministic random seed to reproduce uploader orderings.
Chaos tests: power-loss during fsync and process kill during upload; verify no duplicate credits applied.
Load test: bundle ingestion throughput at 10k events/sec aggregated across 100 tenants to validate server two-phase-apply scaling.
Regression: replay historical private install traces against reconciliation pipeline to ensure no accounting drift.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged server support rolled to staging (1 week), then canary (3 customers), then broad GA if no regressions.
Collector shipped as v0.8 with bundle-v2 enabled behind a config flag; air-gapped customers will be offered migration script and runbook.
Provide a migration tool to convert existing buffered events into signed bundles (idempotent by design).
Console additions released in the same iteration: admin view + reconciliation report link.
notes: PR #4567 contains the merkle implementation and checkpoints; follow-up PR will add KMS signing and bundle rotation. We need security review sign-off before GA to customers on regulated plans.
